newsitem.title: FRANCE: French astronaut to join Russian space mission.
newsitem.headline: French astronaut to join Russian space mission.

text.p: A French astronaut will spend three weeks on the orbiting Russian space station Mir France next August, France announced on Monday.

Astronaut Leopold Eyharts, 39, of Biarritz, southwestern France, will begin training for the mission in Russia next month under an agreement signed in Moscow on Monday, Minister for Space Francois Fillon said.
Jean-Pierre Haignere, the backup astronaut for the mission, has already spent two weeks in space on a Russian mission conducted during July and August 1993.
Under the newly signed agreement, France also will participate in a four-month mission aboard the Mir set for 1999, Fillon said in a statement released in Paris.
Claudie Andre-Deshays, France's first woman in space, returned to earth on September 2 after 16 days aboard the Mir space station where she carried out biological and medical experiments.
